rv.q: Lipton’s compact, tuneful jewel of a play seems charmingly analog...
But taken as a whole, the show, which is directed by Leigh Silverman, feels stifled by slightly monotonous whimsy.
Ethan Lipton’s We Are Your Robots dives headfirst into the Artificial Intelligence conversation with easily the most entertaining theatrical foray into the subject yet.
The ruefully philosophical We Are Your Robots, on the other hand, is a chamber piece that’s as much live concept album or illustrated lecture as stage musical...
In any case, We Are Your Robots will please Lipton's fans and may add a few new ones, too.
If you go into We Are Your Robots expecting to enjoy 80 percent of it, you’ll be just fine.
The show’s content is upbeat for the greater part, and its darkest point is ironically mitigated by comforting assurances and cheerful images of puppies and kittens.
It’s smart, funny, and right in step with the times.
We Are Your Robots will warm your wicked little heart even as it engages your intellect with its cunningly delivered Big Ideas.

The philosophizing that takes place around the ideas of consciousness and what it means be to human, playfully coordinated around some musical robots exploring our needs and wants from them, is tender and kind, but almost too smooth to be enlivening.

cn.t: Critics mostly embrace this whimsical AI musical, praising Lipton's clever concept and jazz quartet format, though some find the execution more charming than powerful. The show earns points for wit and timeliness.

vr.q: The comedic tone of the piece, the design elements, and the music itself all had a charmingly retro feel that was fitting to the themes, and the music was definitely the highlight for me.
